# Editorial Examples — Not Additional Authentic Quotes

The original user-authored paragraph is stored in `VOICE_PROFILE.md`. These are generated *examples of editing strength*; do not cite them as the user's previously written words.

## Meaning that must remain
1. Mathematics may give structure to data analysis.
2. Different methods have different strengths and limitations.
3. Selection should depend on a clear purpose and the available data.
4. Prediction is uncertain; perfect predictive validity cannot be assumed.

## Light grammatical edit
> Data needs a very solid backbone, and I think mathematics can help build it. Different methods have different strengths and limitations, and each method should be evaluated. The role of each method is specific, and it should be used for a clear purpose and with an understanding of the available data. Prediction will still involve uncertainty because, no matter what we do, we cannot expect predictions to be 100% correct.

## Stronger, natural clarity edit
> Data needs a solid backbone, and I think mathematics can help provide it. But different methods work in different ways. Each has strengths and limitations, so what matters is choosing a method for a clear purpose and checking what the data can support. Prediction will still involve uncertainty. Even a well-developed model cannot be expected to predict every situation perfectly.

## Scientific adaptation
> I think mathematical methods give structure to the way we analyze data, but no single method is appropriate for every problem. We should compare their assumptions, strengths, and limitations against the available evidence and intended application. Predictions also require an explicit uncertainty assessment: good performance in one dataset does not establish universal model validity.

The scientific adaptation deliberately changes register; use only if requested. In scientific writing, predictive certainty, error and model validity are related but distinct.

## Bad rewrite — never output
> In today's ever-evolving world, revolutionary mathematical intelligence unlocks an unparalleled data backbone and guarantees superior predictive insights.

Why it fails: exaggerates, invents guarantees, removes uncertainty, and erases the real argument.

## Requested mode → response
- “Fix grammar only” → light edit.
- “Make it clear but keep my voice” → stronger natural clarity edit.
- “Adapt for thesis with high rigor” → scientific adaptation; source-check any new technical claim.
- “Give words/expressions to change” → substitutions only, not a rewritten document.
